name: channel-thread
title: Channel Thread
description: Slack-style chat animation: team messages arrive with typing dots. A work chat filling itself in, the way the channel actually reads: an avatar, a name in bold, a quiet timestamp and the messages as plain lines under them. Messages land one at a time, a second message from the same person joins the group without repeating the name, and when somebody new starts typing three dots hold their line until the words arrive. The transcript never creeps — it sits perfectly still between arrivals and then scrolls, once, by exactly the room the new line needs, and only when the newest line would fall past the anchor. Every vertical number came off a recording and closes on it: carry the layout's arithmetic across the whole scene and it predicts the last frame's baselines to within a pixel.
docs: Docs and props: https://snapcn.dev/docs/text/channel-thread?ref=cli — script is the conversation, groups split by `;` and a group's messages by `|`; people is one `name time` per group; beats is the frame each message lands on and opens is the frame its row appears, so a pause before someone answers is a number rather than a gap you have to guess at. avatars takes one image per group, split by `|` (not by comma — a data: URL has one of its own). Pass mode="dark" if you are rendering onto a dark frame — these default to shadcn's light palette. — 77 Pro components too — charts, launch scenes, device shots: https://snapcn.dev/docs/pricing?ref=cli-docs
